initiative.title: Belt 2200: a solar-system strategy game with real orbits and light lag
initiative.body: Run a faction in a settled solar system where ships obey real orbits, fuel is everything, and every order you send arrives late, at the speed of light. Three powers: the Terran Compact, the Mars Union and the Free Belt, with the Unknown as an optional fourth side. Pitched by Ted on the October 30, 2026 recording. The factions, ships, places, words and story are ours.

milestones.title: First playable
milestones.body: The solar system moving and one ship you send somewhere, playable in the browser and on a phone at openagents.com/realms/belt-2200.

milestones.title: Orrery: the real solar system, Sun to station
milestones.body: Kepler orbits for the bodies, a camera that zooms from the Sun to a station, and a floating origin so nothing jitters.

milestones.title: One ship: plan a transfer, burn, coast, arrive
milestones.body: Patched conics and the transfer planner, with fuel and time shown.

milestones.title: Economy: ice, metal and people
milestones.body: Mine ice and metal, refine at stations, ship it on freighters and build ships.

milestones.title: War: fleets, intercepts and the tactical view
milestones.body: Fleets meet when their paths cross; missiles, rail guns and point defense in a short tactical view.

milestones.title: Light lag: delayed sight and orders
milestones.body: Each faction sees things as they were when their light left; orders take the light time; flagships act on standing orders.

milestones.title: Rivals: AI factions, then lockstep multiplayer
milestones.body: AI opponents in two layers, saves for long campaigns, and deterministic lockstep multiplayer.

tasks.title: First playable at openagents.com/realms/belt-2200
tasks.body: The first version anyone can play: the Sun, the inner planets and a field of named Belt rocks moving on their orbits as time runs, with pause and a time-speed control. Pick your faction's ship at a station, pick a destination, see the planned route with its fuel and travel time, launch, and watch it arrive. A goal for the session: deliver ice from a Belt rock to your capital. Tap to select and long-press for orders on a phone; mouse on desktop. Mark this done when the page plays.
acceptance: https://openagents.com/realms/belt-2200 loads and the planets move on their orbits
A ship can be sent to a Belt rock and back with its fuel and time shown, on desktop and on a phone
The realm is listed or linked from this project's page

tasks.title: Time controls, selection and the route on the map
tasks.body: Pause, three time speeds, tap or click select, and the planned route drawn on the map (burn, coast, arrival) before launch.
acceptance: Pausing stops every orbit and ship
The route is drawn before launch and matches where the ship goes

tasks.title: An ice run: load at a rock, deliver home, score it
tasks.body: Ice is loaded at a Belt rock and counted when delivered to the capital; the session goal and its progress are shown.
acceptance: Delivering a load raises the delivered count
Running out of fuel strands the ship and says so

tasks.title: Play the first version and write down what to fix
tasks.body: Play the first playable on desktop and a phone for ten minutes each and post a note on this task with what to fix (time speed, readability, orders), as new tasks where they are clear.
acceptance: A note on this task lists what was found on desktop and on phone
Each clear fix is a new task in this project

tasks.title: Kepler orbits for the bodies in f64
tasks.body: A new verse/orbit.coax: Kepler orbits from orbital elements for the Sun's planets, Jupiter's and Saturn's major moons and named Belt rocks, scaled for play, in f64 like verse/rigid.coax.
acceptance: coax test verse/orbit.coax passes
A planet's position after one period matches its start to within 1e-9 of its orbit radius in a test

tasks.title: Floating origin, camera-relative drawing and logarithmic depth
tasks.body: The scene spans billions of kilometres and also shows a ship a few hundred metres long. Draw relative to the camera with a floating origin and logarithmic depth so nothing jitters at any zoom.
acceptance: Zooming from the whole system to a 300 m ship shows no jitter or z-fighting in a headless capture

tasks.title: A camera that zooms from the Sun to a station
tasks.body: Smooth zoom and focus from the whole system to one body to one station, with level of detail (as Everglade's) for far bodies.
acceptance: Selecting a station zooms to it in one motion; zooming out returns to the system view

tasks.title: Thousands of Belt rocks, instanced
tasks.body: The Belt as thousands of rocks drawn instanced, with simulation off the main thread, holding 60 frames per second on a phone.
acceptance: 5,000 rocks hold 60 FPS (p95 frame <= 17.5 ms) in the perf run

tasks.title: Patched conics: ships hand off between spheres of influence
tasks.body: Ship trajectories as patched conics with sphere-of-influence handoff, in verse/orbit.coax.
acceptance: A test ship leaving Earth's sphere of influence continues on the matching heliocentric orbit

tasks.title: The transfer planner: go there becomes a burn, a coast and its fuel
tasks.body: Solve Lambert's problem to turn a destination and arrival time into a burn, a coast and the reaction mass it costs; a faster route costs more. A simplified planner first if full Lambert is too heavy on a phone.
acceptance: Planned transfers reach their target within tolerance in tests
A faster arrival always costs more fuel in a test

tasks.title: Plan, launch and follow one ship with fuel and time shown
tasks.body: The first playable's ship flies the planned transfer: the planned burn drawn on the map, a timeline scrubber, and fuel and arrival time.
acceptance: A launched ship follows its drawn route and arrives at the shown time

tasks.title: Ice, metal and people, mined and refined
tasks.body: Mines at rocks and moons produce water ice and metals; stations refine ice into air, water and reaction mass; people crew ships and work stations.
acceptance: A test station turns ice into reaction mass at its rate

tasks.title: Freighters and routes
tasks.body: Set a standing route for freighters between a mine and a station; the cargo moves on real transfers.
acceptance: A standing route keeps delivering without new orders

tasks.title: Build ships from metal and crews
tasks.body: Shipyards at stations build ships from metal and people.
acceptance: Building a ship spends its metal and crew and the ship appears at the yard

tasks.title: Fleets, box select and groups
tasks.body: Box select, control groups and a command queue in verse/command.coax; on phones tap select and long-press for orders (the hotbar's rules).
acceptance: Selecting three ships and giving one order moves all three

tasks.title: Intercepts: fleets meet when their paths cross
tasks.body: Detect when two fleets' trajectories come within combat range and start an engagement.
acceptance: Two crossing fleets in a test start an engagement at the crossing time

tasks.title: The tactical view: missiles, rail guns and point defense
tasks.body: A short tactical battle where ships keep their momentum and turning to fire costs time; missiles burn and coast, rail guns fire straight, point defense shoots missiles down. Then back to the strategic map.
acceptance: A tactical battle resolves and returns to the map with losses applied

tasks.title: Light-lag visibility from a position history
tasks.body: Each faction sees each object as it was distance/c ago: keep a short position history per object and answer where-did-they-see-it queries. The same history serves replay.
acceptance: A test object 10 light-minutes away is seen at its position 10 minutes earlier

tasks.title: Orders arrive late, flagships act on standing orders
tasks.body: Orders to a far fleet take the light time to arrive; a flagship with authority follows its standing orders meanwhile.
acceptance: An order to a fleet 20 light-minutes away takes effect 20 game-minutes later

tasks.title: AI factions: plain code for tactics, the Decisions API for strategy
tasks.body: Tactics (intercepts, point defense, routes) in plain code; strategy (which route to open, when to attack) through our Decisions API (/v1/decisions, Clef first), with every choice logged.
acceptance: A match against two AI factions plays to a win condition
Every strategic choice is in the match log

tasks.title: Save and resume a campaign
tasks.body: Save and resume long campaigns, as Fairy Forest saves (verse/fairy-forest/), only bigger.
acceptance: A saved match resumes with every ship, cargo and orbit where it was

tasks.title: Deterministic lockstep multiplayer with a desync checker
tasks.body: Only orders cross the network; the same orders give the same results on every client. A state hash is compared every few seconds and a desync is reported.
acceptance: Two clients given the same orders have equal state hashes after ten game-days in a test

tasks.title: Win conditions: control the ice, starve a capital, or reach the Unknown
tasks.body: Victory by controlling the ice supply, starving a capital, or, with the Unknown on, reaching it first and holding it. Tune game time so a match is about 45 minutes.
acceptance: Each win condition ends a test match

tasks.title: Pick an ice rock by name, not by a tap among twenty pixels
tasks.body: Playtest (b22-fp-playtest): the eight ice rocks now sit a few degrees along Ceres's orbit, so at the system's scale they and your ships lie within about twenty pixels of Hearth and a tap can't choose one. With a ship selected, show the rocks in reach as a short row of named buttons (name, days, propellant), and let a tap near Hearth zoom in on it.
acceptance: A #test picks each of the eight rocks from the row at 390x844 and at 1280x800
Played on a phone: send RASP to a named rock without zooming

tasks.title: Short hops to rocks beside Ceres: weeks, not 100 to 200 days
tasks.body: Playtest (b22-fp-playtest): every trip to an ice rock beside Ceres takes 100 to 200 days (14 to 28 seconds at 7 D/S) because plan_with's shortest time is 12% of a Hohmann transfer, about 100 days for a near orbit. For a place within a few degrees of the ship on its own orbit, plan from 15 days, so GO FAST is weeks and economy stays cheap.
acceptance: A #test: GO FAST to the nearest rock arrives in under 60 days within RASP's propellant
The existing planner #tests still pass

tasks.title: Something to build with metal after the yard is full
tasks.body: Measured with apps/openagents-web/belt-pace.coax: three ships on MINE ICE bring Hearth about 1,500 t of metal a year. The yard's three freighters (600 t each) are paid for within two years, and after that metal only piles up (43,000 t after a long game). Give it uses: more yard slots, rigs, armour or point defense for KITE, or a station ring that houses more workers.
acceptance: In belt-pace, metal four years in is under 2,000 t for a player who builds what it offers

tasks.title: Ship cards fit a 390 px phone
tasks.body: On a 390x844 phone (dpr 3) the SELECT A SHIP row runs off the right edge: KITE's card is cut after FUEL and its ICE line is gone. Seen on production 2026-10-31 (headless walk). Lay the cards out to the width (narrower cards, or two rows / a scroll) so every card shows whole.
acceptance: A test draws the ship row at 390x844 and 320x568 and every card's box is inside the canvas
